key_insight: Laser post-treatment improved wear resistance in both Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings, while its effects on hardness and elastic modulus depended on the spraying method.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to more wear-resistant sprayed coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel, but stiffness requirements should guide process selection.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying (DS) and gas-flame spraying (GFS), then apply laser post-treatment.
Characterize microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and X-ray diffraction.
Measure mechanical response by instrumented indentation and dry-sliding wear by ball-on-disk testing.
evidence_signal: Wear rates decreased by approximately 24% for DS and 39% for GFS; DS hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, while GFS elastic modulus decreased from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa.
watch_item: The abstract reports dry-sliding performance only, so durability under lubricated, corrosive, or thermally cycled service remains unestablished.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
